labels.text: Run it this once. Tab adds a note for the agent.

S59.01.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider, and an empty test folder
steps: Start agi in an empty test folder.
Type: create a file named notes.txt with one line of text.
At the approval prompt press y (Yes).
Check the file is created and the agent carries on with its reply. Try again and press n instead: the file is not created and the agent carries on.
S59.01.where: agi, then ask the agent to create a file; the approval prompt (Tool Approval) appears in the chat

S59.02.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider, and an empty test folder
S59.02.note: Allow All skips high-risk requests, so some may still prompt.
steps: Type: create three files named a.txt, b.txt and c.txt, each with one line.
At the first approval prompt press t (Allow All), or press d (Deny All) on a second try.
Check the remaining file requests in that turn are approved, or refused, without more prompts.
S59.02.where: agi, then ask for several file changes in one request; the approval prompt has Allow All and Deny All

labels.text: Allow it without asking again until this session ends.

S59.03.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider, and an empty test folder
S59.03.note: Allow Session is not offered for requests that need an explicit decision.
steps: Type: create a file named s1.txt with one line.
At the approval prompt press s (Allow Session).
Type: create a file named s2.txt with one line.
Check no prompt appears for the second file this session. Restart agi and check it asks again.
S59.03.where: agi, then at an approval prompt press s (Allow Session)

S59.04.note: No per-app allow, ask or deny screen was found. MCP tool rules (mcp__<server>__<tool>) are read from a policy.toml file (apps/cli/src/platform/policy/engine.rs lines 357 and 456-464); the in-app /permissions controls cover command prefixes and domain rules only.

labels.text: Directories the agent may read and change.

S59.05.needs: two test folders, one to grant and one not granted
steps: Type /add-dir alone to list the folders the agent may change.
Type /add-dir <path of a test folder> and read the reply.
Ask the agent to create a file in that folder and check it does.
Type /remove-dir <same path>, then ask again and check the agent no longer changes that folder.
S59.05.where: agi, then type /add-dir <folder> and /remove-dir <folder> in the chat

steps: Type /permissions deny domain:example.com and read the reply.
Ask the agent to fetch https://example.com.
Check the fetch is refused and no page content comes back.
Type /permissions remove deny domain:example.com to undo, then ask again and check the fetch is allowed or asked for.
S59.06.where: agi, then type /permissions deny domain:example.com in the chat

S59.07.note: Rules are saved on this computer only, in the AGI config folder; the code has no sync between devices, and agi approvals export and import move them by hand.
steps: In the chat type /permissions allow ls.
Quit agi, then in a terminal run agi approvals list.
Start agi again and type /permissions; check the rule is still listed under Allow.
Check the rule shows in the list from agi approvals list.
S59.07.where: agi, then type /permissions allow <command prefix> in the chat; check later with agi approvals list in a terminal

S59.08.note: Bypass and FullAuto join the cycle only when agi starts with --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions (apps/cli/src/lib.rs). The Shift+Tab help line in screen_renderers.rs says Cycle plan / accept / reject, which is older wording.
steps: Start agi and read the mode badge in the status bar.
Press Shift+Tab once and read the banner and the badge.
Keep pressing Shift+Tab through Plan and Auto, then back to Default.
Check the badge shows the mode you just chose each time.
S59.08.where: agi, then press Shift+Tab to cycle the permission modes

labels.text: read-only tools only, no file edits. The model plans before acting.

S59.09.note: No mode is named read-only; Plan is the closest. Its description does not mention send or execute tools, so check those separately.
steps: Start agi and press Shift+Tab until the badge says Plan.
Read the banner: it says read-only tools only, no file edits.
Type: create a file named p.txt.
Check no file is written and the agent offers a plan instead.
S59.09.where: agi, then press Shift+Tab until the badge says Plan

labels.text: file edits and commands ask first, except read-only ones like ls.

S59.10.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider, and an empty test folder
steps: Start agi and check the badge says Default.
Type: list the files in this folder. It should run without a prompt.
Type: create a file named ask.txt with one line.
Check an approval prompt appears before the file is written.
S59.10.where: agi, in the Default mode (the badge says Default when agi starts)

labels.text: file edits, read-only tools and commands the safety classifier clears run; everything else asks.

S59.11.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider, and an empty test folder
S59.11.note: In Auto, file edits run without asking, which is broader than the item's reads and searches only; compare the real behaviour with Expected.
steps: Press Shift+Tab until the badge says Auto.
Read the banner: file edits, read-only tools and commands the safety classifier clears run; everything else asks.
Type: list the files in this folder. It should run without a prompt.
Type: create a file named auto.txt. Check whether it asks before writing.
S59.11.where: agi, then press Shift+Tab until the badge says Auto

S59.12.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider, and an empty test folder
S59.12.note: No separate line saying why approval is needed was found; the prompt shows the action and its target.
steps: Type: create a file named summary.txt with one line.
At the approval prompt read the first line, which names the tool and the target.
Read the lines under it that show what the change does.
Compare with Expected: the summary says what will happen.
S59.12.where: agi, then ask for a change that needs approval and read the top of the Tool Approval prompt

S59.13.needs: a connected app that can send a message
S59.13.note: A recipients line is built from tool arguments (apps/cli/src/approval_details.rs line 97). The only send tool found in the CLI is send_message for agent teams (apps/cli/src/agent/tools.rs line 10); connector approvals are in apps/cli/src/models/managed_approvals.rs. No send prompt was confirmed in the UI.

labels.text: The agent wants to fetch a page from

S59.14.needs: an internet connection, and a site not already allowed (a prompt appears only then)
S59.14.note: The destination lines are built around apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs line 1532; the cited line 708 was not checked.
steps: Type: fetch https://example.com and summarize it.
At the approval prompt read the destination and address lines.
Check the host and full address match what you typed.
S59.14.where: agi, then ask the agent to fetch a web page; the approval prompt shows the destination

S59.15.note: No payment or purchase tool was found in apps/cli. Amount and What is bought lines are built from tool arguments in apps/cli/src/approval_details.rs lines 99-100, but no prompt that uses them was confirmed.

S59.16.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider
S59.16.note: The command line is shown; where it will run (the working folder) was not confirmed in the overlay code.
steps: Type: run the command ls -la in this folder.
At the approval prompt read the command line under Allow this command?.
Check the command matches what you asked for.
Press n to refuse; the command should not run.
S59.16.where: agi, then ask the agent to run a shell command; the approval prompt shows the command line

S59.17.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider, and an empty test folder
S59.17.note: The prompt names the file; record-level detail was not found.
steps: Type: create a file named records.txt with the line one.
Type: change the word one to two in records.txt.
At the approval prompt read the file path under the prompt line.
Check the path shown is the file that will change.
S59.17.where: agi, then ask the agent to change a file; the approval prompt names the file

labels.text: scroll to the end before allowing

S59.18.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider
S59.18.note: The separate Diff Review screen (/diff-review) is not part of approvals.
steps: Create a test file with several lines first.
Type: change the second line of that file to a new sentence.
At the approval prompt read the lines with + and - in the preview.
Scroll with the arrow keys or PgDn until the end is shown, then press y.
S59.18.where: agi, then ask the agent to edit a file that already has lines; the approval shows the change

labels.text: Run it this once. Tab adds a note for the agent.

S59.19.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider, and an empty test folder
steps: Type: create a file named allow.txt with one line.
At the approval prompt press y.
Check allow.txt is created and the chat shows the result.
S59.19.where: agi, then at an approval prompt press y (Yes)

labels.text: Skip this call; the agent carries on. Tab adds a note saying what to do instead.

S59.20.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider, and an empty test folder
S59.20.note: Whether the model is told the call was denied was not confirmed in the overlay code.
steps: Type: create a file named deny.txt with one line.
At the approval prompt press n.
Check deny.txt is not created and the agent carries on with its reply.
S59.20.where: agi, then at an approval prompt press n (No)

labels.text: Skip this call; the agent carries on. Tab adds a note saying what to do instead.

S59.22.needs: a working AI sign-in or provider, and an empty test folder
steps: Type: create a file named alt.txt.
At the approval prompt press Tab and type: write it to alt-two.txt instead.
Press Enter to answer with the note.
Check the agent follows the note and writes alt-two.txt instead of alt.txt.
S59.22.where: agi, then at an approval prompt press Tab, type a note and press Enter

labels.text: without an answer, so it did not run.

S59.23.needs: about 10 minutes of waiting and a pending approval
S59.23.note: No countdown was found in the overlay; the expiry message in the chat is the only sign.
steps: Type: create a file named late.txt.
Press no key at the approval prompt for 10 minutes.
Check the chat shows: The approval for ... expired after 10 minutes without an answer, so it did not run.
Check late.txt was not created.
S59.23.where: agi, then leave an approval prompt unanswered for 10 minutes

labels.text: Show recent approval decisions, newest first.

S59.24.note: Inside the chat, /permissions recent shows only the Recently denied list.
steps: In agi, approve one request and deny another.
Quit agi and run agi approvals history.
Check the newest decision is listed first and says approved or denied.
Run agi approvals history --limit 1 and check one row is shown.
S59.24.where: a terminal, then agi approvals history

labels.text: Remove a saved or session rule.

steps: Type /permissions allow ls to save a rule.
Type /permissions remove allow ls.
Ask the agent to run ls and check it asks again.
For a folder, type /remove-dir <folder>; for a site, type /permissions remove deny domain:<host>.
S59.25.where: agi, then type /permissions remove allow <command prefix> in the chat

labels.text: List the approvals cloud Code sessions are waiting on.
Approve a waiting cloud Code step, by the handle

S59.26.needs: two signed-in devices and a cloud Code session paused on an approval
S59.26.note: The phone path needs Remote Control running; the cloud path is driven by agi code approve and agi code reject.
steps: Start a cloud Code session that pauses for an approval.
In a terminal run agi code approvals and note the handle.
On a second signed-in device answer the approval, or run agi code approve <handle> in a terminal.
Check the first device shows the result: the chat shows Allowed on your phone or Denied on your phone for a phone answer.
S59.26.where: a terminal, then agi code approvals for cloud Code sessions; the phone path is Remote Control

S59.28.needs: a Free account or a paid account (no sign-in noted in code); a request that makes the agent run a shell command
S59.28.note: Stronger confirmation is in code (requires_explicit_decision hides Allow Session; Always allow hidden for commands without a saved prefix), but the DANGEROUS: line is printed on a non-overlay path (eprintln) so a tester may not see it in the TUI; re-ask on each run was not verified.
steps: Start the app by typing agi in the terminal and wait for the chat prompt.
Type a request that makes the agent run a shell command that needs approval, for example: run sudo ls.
When the Tool Approval prompt opens, look at the buttons: a request that needs explicit decision hides Allow Session, and a command with no saved rule hides Always allow.
Look for the danger wording on the command line (DANGEROUS:) and compare with Expected: a stronger warning, no permanent allow, and the agent asks again next time.
S59.28.where: agi (start the app), then type a chat request that makes the agent run a shell command, such as "run sudo ls", and look at the approval prompt that opens (buttons: Yes, No, Allow Session, Always allow, Deny All, Allow All)

S59.30.needs: none beyond a request that triggers an approval prompt
S59.30.note: The resume behaviour is inner (the parked turn is continued by the broker callback in tui_app.rs); it is visible only as the turn continuing. The phone path ("Allowed on your phone:" in tui_app.rs) depends on Remote Control, which the owner hid in v1.
steps: Start the app by typing agi and send a request that makes the agent change a file or run a command.
When the Tool Approval prompt opens, press y (Yes) or select Yes with the arrow keys and press Enter.
Watch the chat: the same tool row should run and the agent should continue the same reply without a new prompt.
Compare with Expected: the run continues from where it stopped, with no need to send the request again.
S59.30.where: agi (start the app), then type a chat request that needs approval, such as "create a file named test.txt", then at the Tool Approval prompt choose Yes and watch the chat

labels.text: Command was not approved and did not run.

S59.31.needs: none beyond a request that triggers an approval prompt
S59.31.note: The transcript shows the tool outcome and the denial text, but no separate line naming the button chosen was found; the decision itself is not written as its own receipt line.
steps: Start the app by typing agi and send a request that triggers an approval, for example: create a file named test.txt.
At the Tool Approval prompt choose Yes, then choose a second request and choose No.
Look at the tool row in the transcript: a run tool shows its completed state, and a denied call shows the text it did not run.
Compare with Expected: the transcript shows what was decided and what happened (ran, result, or denied).
S59.31.where: agi (start the app), then type a chat request that needs approval, answer the Tool Approval prompt (Yes, No or Deny All), and read the transcript row for the tool
